_meta.codebook: NAMCS public-use file documentation 2015, 2016, 2018, 2019 (record positions in app/etl/namcs_layout.json)
_meta.STATUS: FILLED 27 September 2026. Record positions transcribed from the NCHS documentation for each year and verified field by field against the files (namcs_prepare.py refuses a mismatch). Diagnosis code lists are standard ICD-9-CM and ICD-10-CM categories, listed per concept for clinical-lead review.

design._verified: NCHS NAMCS documentation: PATWT visit weight; CSTRATM masked clustered stratum marker; CPSUM sampled provider marker. CPSUM repeats across years, CSTRATM encodes the year, so nest = TRUE.

sex._note: NAMCS codes SEX 1 = female, 2 = male: the reverse of NHIS and NHANES. Imputed by NCHS where missing (about 1%).

age._note: Age in years, top-coded by NCHS.

phenotype_concepts._instruction: NAMCS concepts are physician diagnoses, not survey answers. Each concept lists ICD code prefixes matched against the five diagnosis fields (DIAGn_CONF: the recorded code, blank when flagged probable, questionable or rule out). The lists cover ICD-9-CM (2015) and ICD-10-CM truncated to 4 characters (2016-2019); ICD-9 codes are numeric and ICD-10 codes start with a letter, so the two never collide. absentIsNegative: no matching code means the condition was not recorded at that visit.

headache_migraine.questionText: Migraine or other headache diagnosis. ICD-10-CM G43 migraine, G44 other headache syndromes, R51 headache; ICD-9-CM 346 migraine, 339 other headache syndromes, 784.0 headache.

dizziness_balance.questionText: Dizziness or vestibular diagnosis. ICD-10-CM R42 dizziness and giddiness, H81 disorders of vestibular function (including BPPV, vestibular neuronitis and Meniere disease), H82 vertiginous syndromes in diseases classified elsewhere; ICD-9-CM 780.4 dizziness and giddiness, 386 vertiginous syndromes. Meniere disease is a MASQUE discriminator in the screener but counts here as a dizziness diagnosis, matching the symptom-level surveys.

hearing_difficulty.questionText: Hearing loss diagnosis. ICD-10-CM H90 conductive and sensorineural hearing loss, H91 other and unspecified hearing loss; ICD-9-CM 389 hearing loss.

tinnitus.questionText: Tinnitus diagnosis. ICD-10-CM H93.1 tinnitus; ICD-9-CM 388.3 tinnitus.

sinus_condition.questionText: Sinusitis diagnosis. ICD-10-CM J01 acute sinusitis, J32 chronic sinusitis; ICD-9-CM 461 acute sinusitis, 473 chronic sinusitis. The first source in which the proposal 7.1 sinonasal arm is expressible.

recalcitrance_proxy._hint: Recalcitrance is repeat courses and persistence across visits. NAMCS samples single visits with no patient linkage, so it cannot be expressed.

caveats: Share of adult physician office visits in which the listed diagnoses were recorded, not a prevalence among people: a patient seen several times counts several times, and a condition not coded at the visit counts as absent.
Physician diagnoses abstracted from the visit record, up to five per visit; codes flagged probable, questionable or rule-out are excluded.
2015 is coded in ICD-9-CM and 2016-2019 in ICD-10-CM truncated to four characters. The code lists cover both, but the transition changes coding detail, so comparability across it is approximate.

Four survey years pooled (2015, 2016, 2018, 2019; 2017 not available) with weights divided by four, so totals are annual averages; proportions are unaffected by the division. Strata (CSTRATM) are year-specific.
Reason-for-visit codes are not used: the reason-for-visit classification list was not in the documentation supplied, so a complaint such as dizziness that was not also diagnosed is not counted.

Estimates are suppressed unless RSE is 30% or less, at least 30 visits are in the denominator, and at least 30 sample visits carry the phenotype (NCHS reliability standard for NAMCS visit estimates, applied to the numerator; stricter than NCHS's 2017 standard for proportions, which this ETL does not implement).
Hypothesis-generating estimate, not a diagnostic count.

eligibility.reason: Adult visits, for comparability with the adult surveys.

phenotype_definition: Adult office visits with a recorded (not probable or rule-out) headache or migraine diagnosis AND a recorded dizziness/vestibular, hearing loss or tinnitus diagnosis at the same visit. The proposal 7.1 phenotype as it appears in physician diagnoses at a single visit; the sinusitis arm is reported separately.
